consulted.title: Installing Pytorch with Python 3.10 for CUDA on NVIDIA TITAN BLACK - TITAN - NVIDIA Developer Forums
consulted.content:
Root cause: conda-forge gcc8’s target triplet is `x86_64-conda-linux-gnu`, its own sysroot doesn’t include Ubuntu’s real `/usr/include`. `--sysroot=/` alone breaks other headers in cascade. Fix: wrapper adds `-isystem /usr/include` only when compiling a file that references `python3.10` (avoid touching the ~750 already-compiled objects against the conda sysroot).

`x86_64-conda-linux-gnu`
`/usr/include`
`--sysroot=/`
`-isystem /usr/include`
`python3.10` [...] Note: when reconfiguring with `cmake ..`, pass BOTH `-DCUDA_HOST_COMPILER=` (PyTorch’s own var) AND `-DCMAKE_CUDA_HOST_COMPILER=` (native CMake var) → both must point to the gcc8 wrapper. One without the other is not enough.

`-DCMAKE_CUDA_HOST_COMPILER=`
